data.narrative:
Zephyr Fusion is a pre-seed stage nuclear energy company founded by two accomplished plasma physicists (Burke: 15+ years in plasma diagnostics at Lawrence Livermore and UW-Madison; Hinson: 20+ years in plasma modeling at Oak Ridge and UW-Madison). The company has raised $500K to date. The nuclear energy sector contains 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private peers including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Deep Atomic.

Stage-progression valuation is the applicable method here. Using total capital raised ($500K) as a proxy for current value and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier for pre-seed to next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $1.25M. Peer-median valuation was not applicable; while 4 nuclear energy peers exist in the broader universe, none met the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation-tier comparables—the threshold of 3+ datapoints required for reliable peer benchmarking was not met.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $1.06M to $1.44M (low to high), centered on $1.25M. The range reflects the stage-progression method's inherent variance but is anchored to a single triangulation point. Key uncertainty centers on access to a sufficiently granular peer set at the pre-seed stage in advanced fission and fusion; broader sectoral comps remain too distant in capital requirements and technology maturity to calibrate this valuation with confidence.
